"Financing is not an end in itself; the real measure is the development it delivers." 

This was at the heart of the dialogue that I co-convened with GEIDCO(Global Energy Interconnection Development and Cooperation Organization) on “Bridging the Gap  Financing a Just and Inclusive Energy Transition.” 

We meet at a moment of paradox. Global clean energy investment will reach $2.2 trillion this year, yet less than 15% flows to developing economies outside China, and Africa, with its vast renewable potential, receives only 2% of that total. The challenge is not if the transition will be financed, but how - and whether it will be just, inclusive, and development-maximizing. From our panel session, three priorities came through strongly: 

🌏 Closing the financing gap through Southern leadership
From Africa’s green industrialization agenda to Asia-Pacific’s blended finance models, countries are already pioneering ambitious national strategies. The task now is to scale and aggregate pipelines to attract capital at the level required. 

🌏 De-risking & financial innovation as drivers of scale  
Sovereign green bonds in Indonesia, sukuk in the Middle East, and guarantee facilities in Africa show how innovative instruments can unlock billions. The next step is replication and mainstreaming. 

🌏 Maximizing development impact through energy investments  
Solarizing clinics in Zimbabwe, electrifying schools in Fiji, and powering farms in Bangladesh show how people-centered finance delivers. The task now is to scale these models so development outcomes define success. 

Grateful to Khaled Sharbatly , @Wang Yao, Pradeep Kurukulasuriya Kurukulasuriya, @Yan Jing, and @Cheng Lin for their insights, and to @Beate Trankmann for reminding us that speed without fairness risks leaving people behind. 

At @UNDP, we believe the energy transition will only succeed if it delivers for people first: lighting homes, powering schools and opening opportunities across the Global South.
